question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's restart-specific durable audit table with redacted source/session/preflight metadata, fixed 512-row retention, and post-transition SQLite writes as the intended product/security boundary?
rationale: The code path is coherent and proved in isolation, but durable operator metadata and restart-path persistence are policy/security choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Accept after conflict refresh
options.body: Refresh the PR against current main and merge if the durable metadata fields, retention cap, and write placement are accepted.

options.title: Narrow stored metadata
options.body: Require a smaller stored column/payload set or stricter redaction contract before merge.

options.title: Fold into broader audit ledger
options.body: Pause or close this PR if restart auditing should wait for a unified audit-ledger direction rather than a restart-specific table.

recommendation.title: Accept after conflict refresh
recommendation.body: Refresh the PR against current main and merge if the durable metadata fields, retention cap, and write placement are accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows broad ownership across restart intent attribution and the database-first state boundary involved in this choice.
